ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) list, the United Nations Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List administered by the US Department of the Treasury, and Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act. Politically exposed persons (PEP) are defined in the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations and require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and senior management approval for high-risk relationships. Continuous monitoring is applied throughout the corporate life cycle.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ontario Business Registry (www.ontario.ca/business-registry); federal equivalent: Corporations Canada online filing centre
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must include a legal element such as 'Limited', 'Incorporated', 'Corporation', or corresponding abbreviations in English or French. Names may be in either official language or both; if the chosen name contains characters outside the Latin alphabet, a transliteration into Latin characters must be provided. The name must be distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing names, trademark-protected names, or names reserved in the Ontario or NUANS search database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal of a proposed corporate name, the applicant may submit a request for reconsideration to the Ontario Business Registry corporate name review officer within 30 days of the refusal, accompanied by additional evidence of distinctiveness, a trademark search report, or the consent of the name holder. If administrative reconsideration is denied, the applicant may apply for judicial review before the Superior Court of Justice under the judicial review procedures of the Ontario Business Corporations Act. For federal incorporation, the equivalent appeal is made to the Director appointed under the Canada Business Corporations Act with a right of further recourse against the Director's decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible in Ontario provided a physical street address within Ontario is maintained for the registered office and is not a post office box, and mail is accepted and directed to the corporation. The address must be an actual location where service of process and government correspondence may be received. Pure mail-forwarding addresses without a physical service location are not acceptable. For federally incorporated corporations, the registered office address must be in Ontario and may use a registered agent's office if the physical location requirement is satisfied.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low likelihood for an automated post-production and AI subtitle studio classified as a standard low-risk commercial activity. Unannounced on-site inspections are rare and typically triggered by regulatory complaints, tax audits, money laundering indicators, or public registry inconsistencies. Estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection is less than 5% for a compliant non-public-facing service company.

B.16 (OBCA), as amended, ss. 1, 3(1), 5, 6, 9, 10, 14, 23, 97, 104, 106, 115, 116, 118(3), 134, 139; O. incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery - ServiceOntario, Ontario Business Registry (companies and personal property branch)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 2 - Articles of Incorporation under the OBCA
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit is required for an OBCA corporation. Shares are issued for consideration fixed by the directors under OBCA s. 23, which may include money, property, or past services; paid-up capital is recorded in the share register and no pre-funded escrow account is required at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation filed under the Ontario Business Corporations Act are ratified; that the share subscriptions tendered by the incorporators are accepted, and the board authorizes issuance of common shares against lawful consideration; that the registered office be established at the address stated in the Articles and, upon filing of the Initial Return, the appointed officers take office; that the individuals named as President, Secretary, and Treasurer are appointed as officers of the Corporation with authority to open banking accounts, execute banking resolutions, and complete statutory filings; that any one officer may execute all documents and attest to corporate records pending ratification by the board. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain NUANS Name Search and Reserve Corporate Name (or Select Numbered Name)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario - Ontario Business Registry (name search module)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search for the proposed corporate name through ServiceOntario. If no name is required, elect to proceed as an Ontario numbered company. For a word-name, verify the legal element (Inc., Corp., Incorporated, Limited), clearly show the corporate name elements, and record the NUANS report number and expiry date. The name reservation is valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search request or numbered-company election
Corporate name elements and legal ending
Incorporator name and contact details
Consent letter of any person or entity whose name/trademark appears in the proposed name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is confusingly similar to an existing registered name, select an alternate name from the NUANS report or file a correction with a fresh NUANS report; ServiceOntario will not register a name causing public confusion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute OBCA Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and legal counsel, submitted through ServiceOntario Ontario Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 2 data within the Ontario Business Registry: registered office address in Ontario, principal place of business if different, share structure and authorized share classes, restrictions, if any, and number of directors. Obtain written consent from each director and ensure at least 25% of directors, or one director if fewer than four, are resident Canadians as required by OBCA s. 118(3). Electronically sign the articles as incorporator.
required_dossiers: Form 2 electronic data (Ontario Business Registry)
NUANS name search report or numbered company number
Director consent to act in office
Registered office street and mailing address
Share capital structure and director information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry identifies a defect, correct the electronic Form 2 before payment or refile after issuance of a notice of correction; the effective date will be the date of the corrected filing unless the registry exercises discretion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles, Pay Fee, and Receive Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the validated Form 2 through the portal, pay the government filing fee by credit card or electronic debit, and download the Certificate of Incorporation once the registry approves the filing. Record the assigned Ontario Business Number/Corporation Number, legal name, and incorporation effective date. Retain the certified Certificate of Incorporation for all subsequent bank, CRA, and municipal licensing steps.
required_dossiers: Validated Form 2 - Articles of Incorporation
Payment of official government filing fee
Incorporator and director signature records
Legal authorization if an agent files
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If incorporation is refused on name, residency, or public-interest grounds, correct the deficiency and resubmit through the same portal. A corrected filing has a new effective date unless ServiceOntario determines that the error was registry-caused.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt First Board Resolution, Issue Shares, and Establish Corporate Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation at its registered office; ServiceOntario to receive any officer or director changes in the Initial Return
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or execute a unanimous written consent in lieu of meeting. Ratify the incorporation, approve the first board resolution, adopt By-Law No. 1 for general governance and By-Law No. 2 for financial matters, authorize share issuance and share certificates, elect officers, and open the registered office. Record all matters in the corporate minute book and issue share certificates from the corporation's securities register.
required_dossiers: Signed first board resolution or consent of directors
General corporate By-Law No. 1 and banking By-Law No. 2
Share certificates and register of shareholders
Officer appointment and acceptance letters
Certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation
Registered office address details and landlord consent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any missing director consent or officer acceptance is cured by obtaining a subsequent written consent with retroactive effect; the minutes may be corrected and ratified at the next board meeting without government penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Initial Return and Register CRA, Ontario Finance, and WSIB Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario - Ontario Business Registry (Initial Return); Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online; WSIB and Ontario Ministry of Finance registration desks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 60 days after incorporation, file the OBCA Initial Return with ServiceOntario giving the registered office and first directors and officers. Through CRA Business Registration Online, open a corporate income tax account; open a GST/HST account if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000; and open a payroll deductions account if employees will be hired. Register with WSIB for mandatory workplace insurance and with the Ontario Ministry of Finance for employer health tax if remuneration thresholds are met. Update the Initial Return on any future address, director, or officer change.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Initial Return information
Director and officer full names, addresses, and resident Canadian status
Corporation fiscal year-end and business activity code NAICS 512191
CRA account registration details and beneficial owner identity information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Initial Return is filed late, file immediately online and correct the registry record; prolonged failure can lead to administrative dissolution under the Corporations Information Act. For CRA accounts, use My Business Account or call Business Registration Online at 1-800-959-5525 to cure activation errors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: City of Toronto Municipal Licensing and Standards Division, Toronto Building, and Toronto Fire Services; Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development; Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Operating Authorization for Non-Major Media Post-Production Facility (non-referenced business category under Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 545, with Zoning and Building Code occupancy approval)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Designated - low-risk commercial post-production, subtitle, and AI voice-cloning studio; no mandatory full Environmental Assessment or EASR registration is triggered by the proposed office and digital studio use unless emergency generators, cooling towers, solvent-based operations, or industrial effluent are added.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary sewage only; any discharge to the municipal sewer must comply with the City of Toronto Sewer Use By-law (Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 681), including pH 6.0-11.5, no process wastewater, and no volatile organic compound discharge to water. If emergency electrical generators are installed, air emissions must meet the maximum point-of-impingement concentration limits under O. Reg. 419/05 (Air Pollution - Local Air Quality) and, if applicable, the Environmental Compliance Approval requirements under the Ontario Environmental Protection Act. Hazardous waste and e-waste must be hauled only to licensed receivers under O. Reg. 347/90 (General - Waste Management).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification to be obtained from Toronto Fire Services under the Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07); structural load and floor capacity inspection plus occupancy certificate closure under the Ontario Building Code (O. Reg. 332/12) if rack systems or acoustic infrastructure are installed; workplace clearance including WSIB registration, OHSA policies, and first-aid and equipment inspection sign-off.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including the CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online portals. The Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers customs and export reporting. Ontario corporate income tax is administered through the CRA under the federal-provincial tax administration framework.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate federally or in Ontario and obtain the certificate of incorporation and corporate legal name. 2. Obtain a CRA Business Number (BN), generally through Business Registration Online, the corporation incorporation process where available, or the CRA non-resident registration process. 3. Register the applicable CRA program accounts: RT for GST/HST, RC for corporate income tax where required, RP for payroll deductions, and RM for import-export activities. 4. For an Ontario corporation, register for GST/HST when the taxable-supplies threshold is exceeded or voluntary registration is selected; registration may be completed by Business Registration Online or by contacting the CRA. 5. A non-resident entity carrying on business in Canada or making taxable supplies in Canada must assess its permanent-establishment, carrying-on-business, GST/HST registration, security, and filing obligations; CRA may request business records, contracts, proof of Canadian activities, and a security deposit. 6. Obtain a nine-digit BN and the relevant fifteen-character CRA program-account identifier, such as the RT GST/HST account. 7. Register for CBSA import-export activities through the CARM Client Portal and obtain the applicable RM account before commercial import or export activity. 8. Maintain legal-name, address, director, authorized-representative, banking, ownership, tax-residency, and transaction records and update CRA and CBSA records promptly after changes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no general U.S.-style check-the-box election for corporations. A Canadian corporation is generally a separate taxable person and files a T2 corporate income tax return. Certain legal forms, including some partnerships, trusts, and unlimited liability entities, may have different classification or filing consequences, but classification is determined under Canadian law and applicable treaty principles rather than by a universal elective form. Canadian hybrid-mismatch rules can deny deductions or impose income inclusions for specified deduction/non-inclusion and imported mismatch arrangements; they do not provide a general elective pass-through classification. A corporation may make specific statutory elections, including elections relevant to tax-deferred transfers, capital cost allowance, foreign-affiliate transactions, and GST/HST methods, but those elections do not convert an ordinary corporation into a pass-through entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST), administered federally by the Canada Revenue Agency. Ontario generally applies Harmonized Sales Tax at the combined federal-provincial rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, excluding zero-rated supplies, measured under the applicable small-supplier rules over the relevant preceding four-calendar-quarter period or in a single calendar quarter. The threshold generally applies on an associated-person and entity-group basis where required. Registration may be voluntary below the threshold. Special rules can require registration for certain non-residents, digital-economy suppliers, taxi and commercial ride services, and other prescribed activities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no general nationwide real-time GST/HST invoice-clearance, mandatory tax-stamping, or continuous transaction-control requirement for ordinary Ontario business-to-business invoices. A GST/HST registrant must issue compliant invoices or receipts when required, showing sufficient information to support tax collection and input tax credits, including the supplier identity and BN/GST/HST account number where applicable, date, description, consideration, tax rate, and GST/HST amount or indication of tax treatment. Electronic records and invoices are permitted if they remain accessible, reliable, readable, and retained for the statutory record-retention period. CRA may require electronic filing or electronic payment for specified registrants and returns, but this is not the same as invoice pre-clearance. CBSA export and import declarations use prescribed electronic systems, including the CARM Client Portal and the Canadian Export Reporting System where applicable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada may generally be zero-rated where the supplier obtains and retains evidence that the goods were exported under the applicable Excise Tax Act rules and were not consumed, used, or supplied in Canada before export. Services supplied to a non-resident may be zero-rated only where the specific statutory conditions are satisfied. The analysis is service-specific: the recipient's non-resident status must be established, the service must generally be supplied to or for the benefit of the non-resident, and exclusions must be tested, including services relating to real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada, services physically performed in Canada for certain purposes, personal services, litigation-related services, and services connected with use or consumption in Canada. Automated subtitle transcription, post-production, dubbing, and AI voice services supplied to a qualifying non-resident may potentially qualify, but the contract, customer location, performance, deliverables, rights of use, and Canadian use or exploitation must be documented and analyzed separately. Export zero-rating does not eliminate the requirement to register where the business makes taxable supplies and does not itself establish entitlement to an input tax refund. GST/HST registrants generally recover eligible GST/HST through input tax credits on their return; non-residents may have separate rebate mechanisms only where statutory conditions apply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Reporting System export declaration or other prescribed CBSA export reporting record, where the goods and transaction are subject to export-reporting requirements
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, purchaser or consignee, description, quantity, value, currency, destination, and terms of sale
Bill of lading, air waybill, courier record, or other carrier-issued transport evidence
Proof of delivery and proof of export, including carrier tracking, export manifest, customs exit confirmation, or foreign import documentation where available
Purchase order, executed contract, customer correspondence, and evidence establishing the non-resident status and foreign destination of the recipient

For exported services, service agreements, work orders, deliverables, time records, customer-location evidence, usage or exploitation evidence, invoices, payment records, and evidence that the service is not excluded from zero-rating
Foreign customs entry or import record where relevant to demonstrate importation into the destination country
Inward remittance or bank payment records where relevant as commercial evidence; Canada does not generally prescribe an Inward Remittance Certificate as a GST/HST zero-rating document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation requirement for GST/HST export zero-rating. Export proceeds may generally remain offshore, subject to ordinary corporate tax, transfer-pricing, foreign-exchange reporting, anti-money-laundering, customs, and banking requirements. CRA may reassess incorrectly zero-rated supplies as taxable, collect the unpaid GST/HST, deny related input tax credits or rebates, and impose arrears interest and applicable penalties. Penalties may include failure-to-file or failure-to-remit penalties, gross-negligence penalties generally calculated at 50% of the understated tax or overstated credit attributable to gross negligence, and other prescribed penalties. False statements, fabricated export evidence, obstruction, or intentional tax evasion may create civil penalties and criminal exposure, including fines and imprisonment. CBSA may separately assess customs penalties, duties, interest, and administrative monetary penalties for inaccurate or unsupported export or import declarations. Records should be retained for the statutory period, generally six years from the end of the relevant tax year, or longer where an objection, appeal, reassessment, or statutory exception applies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains unrestricted convertibility for both current and capital accounts. Corporate profits, dividends, and capital repatriation face no statutory barriers post-taxation. Profit remittance is permitted with only standard withholding tax (25% on dividends to non-residents) and mandatory reporting via CRS/FEAT for non-resident beneficial owners.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds required under Canadian law. Receipts must be reported to the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) within prescribed timelines (typically 30 days for certain transactions exceeding CAD 10,000). Voluntary surrender to the Bank of Canada is available for foreign exchange control purposes but not statutorily mandated.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for fintech electronic money institutions including Wise and Stripe. Legal constraints require FINTRAC registration as a Money Services Business and full compliance with the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote online incorporation and account opening is fully permitted for Canadian corporations. Directors may complete video KYC interviews remotely; physical presence is not mandated except for enhanced due diligence or accounts above CAD 250,000.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions linked to sanctioned jurisdictions, PEPs, or adverse media
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate charter, articles of incorporation, beneficial ownership declaration under the Securities Act, source of funds/wealth evidence, CRA tax clearance certificate, and independent legal opinion on ownership structure

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital via SWIFT MT103 wires using purpose code 848 (Capital Contribution) or 846 (Equity Injection). Verification requires board resolution, share certificate, and ownership proof. Lower-value injections may route through Wise Business or Stripe with reduced documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 for international disbursements or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit through correspondent banks. Post-production service payments (subtitle transcription, AI voice cloning) may settle via Stripe or Wise with proper invoicing and GST/HST compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Annual Return (Business Corporations Act (Ontario), s. 266)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery and Procurement (Ontario), Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (CPSP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after each fiscal year end; no extension is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of approximately CAD 210; failure to file for two consecutive fiscal years triggers a Director's notice under the OBCA and, if unresolved for 60 days after notice, administrative strike-off and dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic penalty for private corporations on late filing; two consecutive unresponded anniversary cycles permit the Director to give notice and dissolve the corporation under the CBCA after 90 days

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Extra-Provincial Annual Return (Corporations Information Act (Ontario), s. 3)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery and Procurement (Ontario), Companies and Personal Property Security Branch
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the Ontario extra-provincial registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fee of approximately CAD 210; two consecutive missed annual returns, after notice, result in revocation of the extra-provincial licence and loss of Ontario contractual standing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year end; balance of corporate income tax due two months after fiscal year end, extended to three months for Canadian-controlled private corporations claiming the small business deduction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per month up to 12 months, increased to 10% for repeated failures; interest accrues daily on unpaid balances under ITA s. 161; continued non-filing permits arbitrary assessment and field audit escalation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is mandatory for CBCA distributing corporations, OBCA offering corporations, and when a shareholder or group of shareholders holding at least 5% of the issued voting shares requests an audit. Private non-distributing corporations may waive the auditor appointment by unanimous shareholder consent; no revenue- or asset-based audit threshold applies for an Ontario private corporation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for publicly accountable and distributing enterprises; a non-distributing private corporation may elect Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). Ontario does not prescribe a separate provincial GAAP for corporate annual filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The CBCA register of individuals with significant control (ISC) must be created, kept current within 15 days of a change, and disclosed to Corporations Canada; Ontario annual return filings require confirmation of ISC particulars and any transfer resulting in a person holding at least 25% voting rights or equivalent de facto control. On share transfers, the Ontario and federal register of members must be updated contemporaneously and the ISC register must record the transferor's and transferee's significant control details.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book, Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - 30,000 per full audit cycle for a small private post-production corporation; USD 3,500 - 7,000 for a review engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal + Ontario general corporate rate (federal 15% + Ontario 11.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction reduces combined rate to 12.2% on the first C$500,000 of active business income (federal 9% + Ontario 3.2%); SR&ED refundable investment tax credits of 35% on qualifying CPD expenditures for CCPCs; federal Film or Video Production Services Tax Credit of 16% and Ontario Production Services Tax Credit of 18% on qualifying Canadian labour for eligible post-production services rendered to non-resident producers; Ontario Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit historically available but terminated — confirm current provincial program status at filing time.
